scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The imported label Anhalt covers snapshots from 1783 to 1878 with areas near the middle Elbe and Harz. Its imported Wikipedia lead points to Saxony-Anhalt, which is not an identical state. The narrative explicitly separates the principalities, 1863 duchy, republican administration and postwar regional reorganization.
No early founding date or precise sovereignty interval is inferred from the imported geometry. The card uses dated phases and leaves unsupported intervals without a fabricated selected-year account.

The archival summary gives 1797 in a compressed discussion of the Zerbst branch, while other histories distinguish the ruler’s death in 1793 from territorial partition. Neither date is used as a simplified extinction claim here.
The scholarly language project’s indexed Köthen-period text was read. Its 1624 discussion is attributed rather than presented as a complete theory of German standardization.
Bach’s employer and service dates are supported by the local Bach organization. The card avoids assigning disputed composition dates or entire collections to Köthen without manuscript research.

Garden Kingdom is a modern descriptive name for a designed landscape, not a separate sovereign kingdom. UNESCO’s significance statement supports the relationship among education, agriculture, architecture and engineering; universal first-invention claims are omitted.

The synagogue pages vary on the final year of religious use and describe its geometrical precedent inconsistently. These disputed details are omitted. Shared facts used here are the 1789 to 1790 construction, surviving mikveh and 1938 destruction of furnishings.

The parliament-building publication’s indexed section 9.2 was read for the 1918 abdication. Its scanned pages were not visually examined. Kettmann’s later parliamentary work comes from the legislature’s separate historical article.

Bauhaus architecture is placed after the monarchy, within the later regional narrative. The foundation’s observed Haus Anton fittings and account of affordability are retained; no claim says every worker could buy a house or every building remains original.

The archive’s specific 1945 chronology takes precedence over compressed summaries that merge formation with the 1946 renaming. No successor link is made without independently verified event-year map geometry.
Independent historical review, border verification and depth certification remain pending.
